items.q: Which Maven artifact brings in Rest Assured?
items.e: io.rest-assured:rest-assured — the official artifact since version 3.x (moved from com.jayway).

items.q: What is the BDD-style structure of Rest Assured?
items.e: given() / when() / then() — the Rest Assured BDD structure: preconditions, action, verification.

items.q: How do you send a GET request in Rest Assured?
items.e: given().when().get(url) is the standard way. Plain get(url) also works with a static import.

items.q: How do you assert the response status code?
items.e: then().statusCode(200) — asserts the HTTP status code of the response.

items.q: How do you set the base URL for all requests?
items.e: RestAssured.baseURI = "https://api.example.com" — the global base URL setting.

items.q: How do you set the base port?
items.e: RestAssured.port = 8080 sets the port for all requests.

items.q: How do you add a header to a request?
items.e: given().header("Name", "Value") adds an HTTP header to the request.

items.q: How do you add several headers at once?
items.e: headers(Map) and headers("k1","v1","k2","v2") — both add multiple headers.

items.q: How do you set Content-Type: application/json?
items.e: contentType(ContentType.JSON) or contentType("application/json") — both are correct.

items.q: How do you pass a request body?
items.e: given().body(object) — passes the request body. Serialized automatically when Jackson/Gson is on the classpath.

items.q: How do you make a POST request?
items.e: when().post(url) — sends a POST request to the given endpoint.

items.q: How do you make a PUT request?
items.e: when().put(url) — sends a PUT request.

items.q: How do you make a DELETE request?
items.e: when().delete(url) — sends a DELETE request.

items.q: How do you make a PATCH request?
items.e: when().patch(url) — sends a PATCH request for a partial update.

items.q: How do you extract a field value from a JSON response by path?
items.e: extract().path("field") and jsonPath().get("field") — both pull a value out of the JSON response.

items.q: How do you assert a field value in a JSON response?
items.e: then().body("field", equalTo("value")) — field assertion using a Hamcrest matcher.

items.q: How do you check that an array contains an item?
items.e: hasItem() — the Hamcrest matcher that checks an element is present in a collection.

items.q: How do you extract the whole response body as a string?
items.e: extract().body().asString() returns the response body as a String.

items.q: How do you deserialize a response into a Java object?
items.e: extract().as(Class) and extract().body().as(Class) — both deserialize JSON into a Java object.

items.q: What is RequestSpecification?
o: A request template with pre-configured parameters
items.e: RequestSpecification — an object with pre-configured headers, baseURI, contentType etc. for reuse.

items.q: How do you create a RequestSpecification?
items.e: RequestSpecBuilder builds a specification which is then passed to given().spec(spec).

items.q: What is ResponseSpecification?
o: A reusable template for response assertions
items.e: ResponseSpecification — a set of response assertions reusable via then().spec(spec).

items.q: How do you add a query parameter?
items.e: queryParam() and param() — both add query parameters to the URL (?key=value).

items.q: How do you add a path parameter?
items.e: pathParam("id", 5) substitutes the value into the URL template: "/users/{id}" → "/users/5".

items.q: How do you configure Basic authentication?
items.e: given().auth().basic("username", "password") — automatically adds the Base64-encoded Authorization header.

items.q: How do you configure Bearer token authentication?
items.e: auth().oauth2(token) and header("Authorization","Bearer "+token) — both work for Bearer auth.

items.q: How do you disable SSL certificate validation?
items.e: useRelaxedHTTPSValidation() globally or relaxedHTTPSValidation() per request — both disable SSL validation.

items.q: How do you assert a response header?
items.e: then().header("Content-Type", "application/json") — asserts a response header value.

items.q: What is JsonPath in Rest Assured?
o: A library for navigating JSON structures
items.e: JsonPath lets you navigate the JSON response using Groovy GPath expressions.

items.q: How do you get a list of values from a JSON array?
items.e: getList("items.name") and get("items[*].name") — both return a List of the field values from an array.

items.q: What is XmlPath in Rest Assured?
o: The JsonPath analog for XML responses
items.e: XmlPath navigates XML responses via GPath expressions, just like JsonPath does for JSON.

items.q: How do you log the request in Rest Assured?
items.e: given().log().all() logs all request details: URL, headers, body. Also log().headers(), log().body() etc.

items.q: How do you log the response?
items.e: then().log().all() logs all response details. log().ifError() logs only on error.

items.q: How do you log only when a test fails?
items.e: log().ifValidationFails() — best practice: logs the request/response only when the assertion fails.

items.q: How do you set the connection timeout?
items.e: HttpClientConfig with the CoreConnectionPNames.CONNECTION_TIMEOUT or SO_TIMEOUT parameter sets the timeout.

items.q: How do you assert the size of an array in a JSON response?
items.e: body("list.size()", equalTo(3)) (GPath) and body("list", hasSize(3)) (Hamcrest) — both check the size.

items.q: What is RestAssured.filters()?
o: Filters for intercepting and modifying requests/responses
items.e: Filters allow you to intercept, modify or log requests and responses globally.

items.q: What is RequestLoggingFilter?
o: A filter that logs only requests
A filter that logs requests and responses
items.e: RequestLoggingFilter logs request details. Together with ResponseLoggingFilter it covers the full HTTP traffic.

items.q: How do you send form data (form params)?
items.e: formParam("key","value") — for application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests.

items.q: How do you upload a file as multipart?
items.e: multiPart("file", new File(path)) adds the file as a multipart/form-data part of the request.

items.q: How do you assert the response time?
items.e: then().time(lessThan(2000L)) — asserts the response time is below the given value in milliseconds.

items.q: What is ResponseBody.prettyPrint()?
o: Prints the formatted response to the console
Saves the response to a file
items.e: prettyPrint() prints the response in formatted form to the console and returns it as a string.

items.q: How do you store the response for later use?
items.e: extract().response() returns a Response object for further use outside the chain.

items.q: What is ObjectMapping in Rest Assured?
items.e: ObjectMapping automatically serializes objects to JSON/XML for requests and back for responses (via Jackson, Gson etc.).

items.q: How do you configure Jackson for serialization?
items.e: objectMappingConfig with jackson2ObjectMapperFactory lets you customize the ObjectMapper globally.

items.q: What is the Hamcrest matcher equalTo()?
o: Checks that an object is null
items.e: equalTo(value) — the Hamcrest matcher for exact equality. Used in body() assertions.

items.q: What is the Hamcrest matcher containsString()?
o: Checks that a string contains a substring
Checks that a collection contains an element
items.e: containsString("text") checks that the string contains the given substring.

items.q: What is the Hamcrest matcher notNullValue()?
o: Checks the value is not null and not empty
Checks the value is not null
Checks the string is not empty
Checks the list is not empty
items.e: notNullValue() checks the value is not null. For a non-empty string use not(emptyString()).

items.q: How do you assert several fields at once?
o: Several then() calls in one request
items.e: then().body("f1", equalTo(v1)).body("f2", equalTo(v2)) — multiple body() assertions in a single chain.

items.q: How do you validate a response against a JSON Schema?
items.e: matchesJsonSchema(File/String) — validates the response against a JSON Schema. Needs the json-schema-validator module.

items.q: Which artifact is needed for JSON Schema validation?
items.e: io.rest-assured:json-schema-validator — the official Rest Assured module for JSON Schema validation.

items.q: How do you send a request with cookies?
items.e: cookie("name","value") and cookies(Map) — both work for passing cookies in a request.

items.q: How do you get a cookie from the response?
items.e: response.cookie("name") and response.getCookie("name") — both return the cookie value from the response.

items.q: What is RestAssured.reset()?
o: Resets all global RestAssured settings to defaults
items.e: RestAssured.reset() resets baseURI, basePath, port and all other global settings to their defaults.

items.q: What is basePath in RestAssured?
o: A base path appended to every URL
items.e: RestAssured.basePath = "/api/v1" — inserted between baseURI and the endpoint in every request.

items.q: How do you pass a JSON string as the request body?
items.e: body(String) with contentType(ContentType.JSON) — passes the JSON string as the body with the right Content-Type.

items.q: What is GPath in Rest Assured?
o: A Groovy-based syntax for navigating JSON and XML
items.e: GPath — the Groovy navigation syntax Rest Assured uses in JsonPath and XmlPath.

items.q: How do you check that a field exists in JSON?
items.e: body("field", notNullValue()) — if the field exists, it is not null. For absence: body("field", nullValue()).

items.q: How do you get the response status code?
items.e: response.statusCode() and response.getStatusCode() — both return the HTTP status code as an int.

items.q: How do you get a response header?
items.e: response.header("Name") and response.getHeader("Name") — both return the response header value.

items.q: What is SerenityRest?
o: Rest Assured integrated with Serenity BDD for reporting
items.e: SerenityRest — a wrapper over Rest Assured that adds Serenity BDD steps and automatic reporting.

items.q: How do you send a request through a proxy?
items.e: given().proxy() or RestAssured.proxy() — HTTP proxy configuration for requests.

items.q: What is RestAssuredConfig?
o: The global configuration object for all Rest Assured aspects
items.e: RestAssuredConfig combines all configurations: SSL, ObjectMapping, Connection, HttpClient and more.

items.q: How do you configure DecodeContentConfig?
items.e: DecoderConfig configures response decoding, e.g. GZIP or DEFLATE.

items.q: What is io.restassured.module.mockmvc?
o: A module for testing Spring MVC without starting a server
items.e: rest-assured-spring-mock-mvc lets you test Spring MVC controllers through MockMvc without HTTP.

items.q: How do you check that the response body is empty?
items.e: emptyString() and isEmptyString() (deprecated) — Hamcrest matchers for an empty body.

items.q: What is ContentType.JSON in Rest Assured?
items.e: ContentType.JSON — the Rest Assured enum constant for "application/json; charset=UTF-8".

items.q: How do you get all response headers?
items.e: response.headers() and response.getHeaders() — both return a Headers object with all headers.

items.q: How do you assert the response content type?
items.e: contentType(ContentType.JSON), contentType("application/json") and the header check — all are valid.

items.q: What is ResponseSpecBuilder?
o: A builder for creating a ResponseSpecification
A builder for the server response
A class for modifying the response
items.e: ResponseSpecBuilder builds a ResponseSpecification — a reusable set of assertions applied via then().spec().

items.q: How do you check that a JSON field is a number?
items.e: isA(Integer.class) and instanceOf(Integer.class) — Hamcrest matchers for type checking.

items.q: How do you assert a nested object field?
items.e: body("user.address.city", equalTo("Kyiv")) — GPath supports dot notation for nested fields.

items.q: What is the io.restassured.path.json.JsonPath class?
o: A utility for parsing JSON without an HTTP request
items.e: JsonPath.from(jsonString).get("field") — you can parse a JSON string without making a request.

items.q: How do you configure preemptive Basic auth?
items.e: preemptive().basic() sends credentials immediately without waiting for a 401, unlike plain basic().

items.q: What is Digest auth in Rest Assured?
items.e: auth().digest("user","pass") — HTTP Digest authentication, safer than Basic.

items.q: How do you use OAuth 1.0?
items.e: auth().oauth(consumerKey, consumerSecret, accessToken, secretToken) — OAuth 1.0 request signing.

items.q: How do you check that an array is in exact order?
items.e: contains(1,2,3) checks the exact order and content. hasItems checks presence regardless of order.

items.q: What is the AllureRestAssured filter?
o: A filter that adds HTTP steps to the Allure report
items.e: new AllureRestAssured() — a Rest Assured filter that automatically attaches requests/responses to the Allure report as steps.

items.q: How do you attach AllureRestAssured?
items.e: Add it globally via RestAssured.filters() or per request via given().filter().

items.q: How do you set the request encoding?
items.e: EncoderConfig.encoderConfig().defaultContentCharset("UTF-8") sets the request body encoding.

items.q: What is redirect handling in Rest Assured?
o: Redirecting the request to a proxy
A redirect pattern in the URL
items.e: By default Rest Assured follows redirects automatically. Disable via redirects().follow(false).

items.q: How do you disable automatic redirects?
items.e: redirectConfig().followRedirects(false) or given().redirects().follow(false) — both disable auto-redirects.

items.q: How do you send a multipart request with a JSON body part?
items.e: multiPart with an explicit content type lets you send a JSON part together with a file in a multipart request.

items.q: What is RestAssured.given() vs given()?
o: The same — given() with a static import
RestAssured.given() — a new session, given() — the existing one
given() supports fluent API, RestAssured.given() doesn't
items.e: given() with static import io.restassured.RestAssured.* — the same as RestAssured.given(). Just cleaner syntax.

items.q: How do you check that a response field matches a regex?
items.e: matchesRegex("regex") — the Hamcrest matcher for matching a string against a regular expression.

items.q: What about soft assertions in the context of Rest Assured?
o: An external library is needed (AssertJ, JUnit5)
items.e: Rest Assured has no built-in soft assertions. Use AssertJ SoftAssertions or JUnit5 assertAll() together with extract().

items.q: How do you validate a response against an XML Schema (XSD)?
items.e: matchesXsd(String/File) — validates the XML response against an XSD schema. The XML analog of matchesJsonSchema.

items.q: How do you get the response time after a request?
items.e: response.time() and response.timeIn(TimeUnit) — both return the response time in different units.

items.q: What is RequestSpecification.when()?
o: The transition to the HTTP method
items.e: when() finishes the request setup (given()) and moves on to choosing the HTTP method (get, post etc.).

items.q: How do you set a proxy globally?
items.e: RestAssured.proxy("host", port) sets the HTTP proxy for all subsequent requests globally.

items.q: What is io.restassured.module.webtestclient?
items.e: rest-assured-spring-web-test-client — Rest Assured integration with Spring WebFlux via WebTestClient.

items.q: What is the ResponseOptions interface?
o: The base interface of Response and ValidatableResponse
items.e: ResponseOptions — the base interface defining the common methods of Response and ExtractableResponse.

items.q: How do you persist cookies between requests?
items.e: SessionFilter automatically stores and passes cookies between requests — handy for login-based testing.

items.q: What does extract().response() return?
o: A Response object for use outside the chain
items.e: extract().response() exits the fluent chain and returns the Response object for further operations.

items.q: How do you check that a list contains exactly certain items (no extras)?
items.e: containsInAnyOrder checks the exact set regardless of order. contains — the same but with order.

items.q: What is the difference between contains() and hasItems() in Hamcrest?
o: contains — exact set and order, hasItems — presence only
contains for arrays, hasItems for lists
items.e: contains() checks the exact content and order. hasItems() only checks the given items are present (others allowed).

items.q: How do you send a PUT request with an empty body?
items.e: given().when().put(url) without body() sends a PUT with an empty body.

items.q: What is io.restassured.specification.RequestSender?
o: The interface providing get(), post(), put() etc.
A wrapper over the HTTP client
items.e: RequestSender — the interface returned by when(), providing the HTTP methods: get, post, put, delete, patch etc.
